testDefinitions.notes: Sample solution 100 mg/mL. To 1 mL add 5 mL 1 N NaOH and 1 drop cupric sulfate TS; shake vigorously: deep blue colour develops. USP Monograph for Dexpanthenol (source: Panthenol__Panthenol - SM 1.txt:30).

testDefinitions.displayName: Identification (hydroxylamine and ferric chloride reaction, D-Panthenol)
testDefinitions.notes: Sample solution 10 mg/mL. To 1 mL add 1 mL 1 N HCl, heat on steam bath 30 min, cool, add 100 mg hydroxylamine hydrochloride and 5 mL 1 N NaOH, stand 5 min, adjust to pH 2.5-3.0 with 1 N HCl, add 1 drop ferric chloride TS: purplish red colour develops. USP Monograph for Dexpanthenol (source: Panthenol__Panthenol - SM 1.txt:30).

Dissolve 5 g sample in 10 mL water, add bromothymol blue TS, titrate with 0.01 N sulfuric acid VS to yellow endpoint. Blank determination with 10 mL water. Result % = [((VS - VB) x N x F) / W] x 100; F = 75.11 mg/mEq; W = sample weight in mg. USP <541> Titrimetry (source: Panthenol__Panthenol - SM 1.txt:31).

400 mg sample in 300-mL flask + 50.0 mL 0.1 N perchloric acid VS, reflux 5 h, cool, rinse condenser with glacial acetic acid, add 5 drops crystal violet TS, back-titrate with 0.1 M potassium biphthalate to blue-green endpoint. Blank determination without sample. Result % = {[(VB - VS) x M x F] / [W x (100 - WC)]} x 100 x 100; F = 205.3 mg/M; W in mg; WC = water content (anhydrous basis row). USP <541> Titrimetry. Note: titrant 0.1 M Potassium biphthalate VS is complete: false (no standardization procedure stated in STM; source: Panthenol__Panthenol - SM 1.txt:36).
testDefinitions.heldBack: titrant 0.1 M Potassium biphthalate VS has no standardization; see held-back report

testDefinitions.displayName: Identification (pH of solution, Citric Acid Monohydrate)
testDefinitions.notes: Dissolve 1.0 g in 10 mL water: solution is strongly acidic. BP Monograph for Citric Acid Monohydrate (source: Citric acid Monohydarte__Citric acid Monohydarte -SM.txt:29).

testDefinitions.displayName: Identification (reaction with acetic anhydride and pyridine, Citric Acid Monohydrate)
testDefinitions.notes: Add ~5 mg to a mixture of 1 mL acetic anhydride and 3 mL pyridine: red colour develops. BP Monograph for Citric Acid Monohydrate (source: Citric acid Monohydarte__Citric acid Monohydarte -SM.txt:29).

testDefinitions.displayName: Identification (calcium chloride precipitation, Citric Acid Monohydrate)
testDefinitions.notes: Dissolve 0.5 g in 5 mL water, neutralise with 1 M NaOH (~7 mL), add 10 mL calcium chloride solution: remains clear. Boil: white precipitate forms, soluble in dilute HCl. BP Monograph for Citric Acid Monohydrate (source: Citric acid Monohydarte__Citric acid Monohydarte -SM.txt:29).

To 1.0 g in test tube add 10 mL sulfuric acid, heat in water bath at 90 ± 1 °C for 60 min, cool rapidly. Solution is not more intensely coloured than a mixture of 1 mL red primary solution and 9 mL yellow primary solution. BP Appendix IV B (source: Citric acid Monohydarte__Citric acid Monohydarte -SM.txt:32).

testDefinitions.displayName: Assay of Citric Acid Monohydrate (acid-base titration)
testDefinitions.titrationEquivalencyFactorDerivation: stated: 1 mL 1 M NaOH = 64.03 mg C6H8O7 / 1 = 64.03 mg/mmol
testDefinitions.notes: 0.550 g in 50 mL water, titrate with 1 M sodium hydroxide VS using 0.5 mL phenolphthalein solution as indicator. 1 mL 1 M NaOH = 64.03 mg C6H8O7. Result calculated on anhydrous basis using water content WC: (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100 x 100) / [Wt x (100 - WC)]. BP 2024 Monograph for Citric Acid Monohydrate (source: Citric acid Monohydarte__Citric acid Monohydarte -SM.txt:37).

solutions.name: 0.1 M Potassium biphthalate VS
solutions.instructions: Transfer 20.42 g of potassium biphthalate into a 1000-mL volumetric flask and add sufficient glacial acetic acid to dissolve. Cool to room temperature, and dilute with glacial acetic acid to volume.
solutions.notes: Transfer 20.42 g potassium biphthalate into a 1000-mL volumetric flask, dissolve in and dilute to volume with glacial acetic acid. Used as back-titrant in Dexpanthenol assay. Complete: false because STM states no standardization procedure (prepared directly from primary standard), shelf life, or storage condition (source: Panthenol__Panthenol - SM 1.txt:26).

solutions.name: 1 M Sodium hydroxide VS
solutions.instructions: Dissolve 42 g of sodium hydroxide in carbon dioxide-free water and dilute to 1000.0 mL with the same solvent. Standardize against 1.50 g of potassium hydrogen phthalate in 50 mL of water, using 0.1 mL of phenolphthalein solution as indicator (1 mL 1 M NaOH = 204.2 mg potassium hydrogen phthalate).
solutions.notes: 42 g sodium hydroxide dissolved in carbon dioxide-free water to 1000.0 mL. Standardized against 1.50 g potassium hydrogen phthalate in 50 mL water, 0.1 mL phenolphthalein solution (1 mL 1 M NaOH = 204.2 mg KHP). House defaults applied: 3 replicates, factor 0.98-1.02 for 1 M titrant, max RSD 0.2 %, validity 30 days, shelf life 30 days, storage condition "Tightly closed, room temperature" (source: Citric acid Monohydarte__Citric acid Monohydarte -SM.txt:26).
